**Current behavior**
<!-- Describe how the bug manifests. -->
I was following the Upgrade documentation to upgrade an Angular1 Component to Angular2:
https://angular.io/docs/ts/latest/guide/upgrade.html

When using `@angular 2.2.1`'s `UpgradeComponent`, it gives an error saying this.$injector is not found in `upgrade_component.js`

![screen shot 2016-11-18 at 12 01 42](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/2917613/20430650/7d42f6e4-ad8d-11e6-87b8-40d5636971b4.png)

Upon closer inspection... Line 97 of `upgrade_component.js` is `undefined`:
![screen shot 2016-11-18 at 12 02 59](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/2917613/20430678/a1144dde-ad8d-11e6-9ae5-f2c858ef1720.png)

**Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions**
Minimal Demo is created using `angular-cli`, with only **one** filed added: https://github.com/dolanmiu/angular2-upgrade-test
https://github.com/dolanmiu/angular2-upgrade-test/blob/master/src/app/chart/chart.component.ts

The corresponding `.ts` file is here:
https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/modules/@angular/upgrade/src/aot/upgrade_component.ts#L121

**What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior?**
<!-- Describe the motivation or the concrete use case -->
I **need** to upgrade old existing Angular1 code into Angular2

body: I'll take a look early next week unless @gkalpak  gets to it first ;-)
This happens also in an upgraded component too.
Sorry. It is on my todo list. Hopefully I will have some time later today.

As a starter I don't think that we will be able to support

1. Service having ngOnInit lifecycle method. When you put it on a ng2 service that injects upgraded services, factory for this upgraded service is called sooner (during bootstrapModule, not in upgrade.bootstrap as it should, so $injector is not available).

The design of upgrade is that the Angular module bootstraps before the AngularJS module, so if your Angular module provides services that have `ngOnInit` hooks then they will be called before we even begin to create the AngularJS injector. One workaround for this might be to lazy load the modules that have such services after the bootstrap of AngularJS has completed.

I think we ought to do better for scenario 2 - I'll look into it over the weekend.
I am not sure I understand scenario 3 - can you provide a plunker or more concrete reproduction steps?

I think scenario 2 is basically the same as scenario 3 (i.e., by fixing 2 we get 3 fixed as well). I don't currently have access to the project that demonstrated this, so I wouldn't be probably able to provide a working plunker. I'm able to do this on the next Tuesday if that is necessary.

Impossibility of fixing 1: I think this should be mentioned in the documentation (https://angular.io/docs/ts/latest/guide/upgrade.html).

OK, so I think I know the cause of the problem.  If you look here: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/modules/%40angular/upgrade/src/aot/upgrade_module.ts#L156

You can see that we create an AngularJS (1.x) upgrade module, which

a) depends upon the `modules` passed into the call to bootstrap
b) has a run block that initializes the upgraded injector service

The problem is that AngularJS will run the `run` blocks for dependent modules before the `run` blocks of the current module. So the injector has not been initialized by the time the modules' run blocks are executed.

I think we can solve this by creating two modules. A new one that simply initializes the injector and then the main upgrade module that puts that new module at the front of its dependencies list.

This change ensures that the upgraded AngularJS injector is initialized
before the application run blocks are executed.

Closes #13811


**What is the current behavior?** (You can also link to an open issue here)

The upgraded injector is initialized in a run block that is executed after the application's run
blocks are executed, which means that this injector is not available to downgraded Angular
services that are used in AngularJS run blocks.

**What is the new behavior?**

The injector is now initialized before the application run blocks are executed.

body: Please take a look at #14065 as a potential solution
I can confirm that both 2 and 3 scenarios are fixed by #14065.

And for scenario 1, I found that I'm not actually sure what is a correct application code (i.e., whether the provided plunker is a valid code). Lifecycle hooks are documented just for directives and components, but not for services. However, at least ngOnInit is called for services. Providing this method causes the service to be created sooner (and this lifecycle hook to be called during application bootstrap). When omitting the hook (and doing the same job in costructor, for instance), the service is instantiated later.

I don't see anywhere in the documentation whether a service should do its initialization job in constructor or in ngOnInit (for components, constructor approach is clearly a bad practice).
